Hi Alex,

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap and the SLO checklist we discussed attached. High level points we agreed/covered on the call:

- Target latency: you mentioned the product goal is p95 end-to-end <100ms for single-turn short prompts (<= 128 tokens) and p95 <250ms for longer streaming sessions (<= 512 tokens).
- Concurrency: initial expected concurrency ~200 concurrent users (peak), with burst to ~500 for short windows.
- Throughput: steady-state QPS target around 60 qps, burst to 150 qps.
- Streaming: you want partial tokens streamed to the client within 50-150ms of generation (per-chunk), and overall keep-first-byte latency visible in dashboards.
- Decision criteria for POC: meet p95 latency targets under synthetic load 90-95% of the time, <2% error rate, and cost within the target range we discussed.

Next steps / MAP items:
1) We'll share an SLO checklist + sample test plan (attached) - owner: me - by EOD today.
2) Redwood tech to validate target numbers and recommend config (Dedicated vs Hosted) - owner: Aditya - by EOD tomorrow.
3) Agree on POC scope, duration (2 weeks recommended), success criteria - owner: Alex/Sarah - goal: sign-off this week.
4) Provisioning & test data plan - owner: FinTechCo infra/procurement - coordinate with Rishi.

Please review the attached checklist and flag any corrections. We'll pull together the configuration recommendation (batching, model variant, quantization profile) and a short runbook for the POC.

Marissa, thanks for the recap and the attachment. A couple clarifying points from our side so we can sign off on the MAP: 

- Latency: the <100ms p95 target is for the UI micro-interaction (single-turn) where users type short prompts (~30-50 tokens). For generation flows up to 512 tokens we are OK with p95 <250ms, but we do expect streaming chunks to arrive frequently so UX feels fluid. Can you confirm whether that 50-150ms per-chunk streaming latency is measured from token generation on the model or from first-byte to client (including network)?
- Concurrency: 200 concurrent users is an average; we anticipate spikes up to 800 concurrent during market opens. How does Redwood recommend headroom planning (safety factor)?
- Throughput: our procurement timeline is tight - we need a short statement of expected unit costs for Hosted vs Dedicated for budgeting.

Hey Alex - quick technical answers to the bullets below and recommended config for the POC.

1) Streaming latency definition: we measure per-chunk first-byte latency end-to-end (model generation -> network egress -> client receive). For most deployments on us-west GPUs and typical AWS networking, per-chunk 50-150ms is achievable for small chunks (8-16 tokens) with a Dedicated pool and continuous batching disabled for low-latency routes. Hosted will be slightly higher variance.

2) Latency targets & model advice:
- Short prompts (<=128 tokens): target p95 <100ms - achievable with Dedicated + optimized kernel selection and kv-cache warmup.
- Long streaming sessions (<=512 tokens): target p95 <250ms - achievable but depends on chunk size and batch policy. We recommend chunk sizes of 8-16 tokens for best UX.

3) Concurrency & headroom:
- For 200 concurrent users (steady): plan for 2-3 model workers per 100 concurrent sessions depending on model size (e.g., Llama-2-70B quantized). For spikes to 800, recommend autoscale policy to add burst nodes; safety factor 2-3x capacity for market-open bursts.

4) Throughput & cost guidance:
- Expected steady QPS 60: Dedicated pool (reserved) cost estimate: see short table below (ballpark):
  * Dedicated (reserved): $X,XXX/month per node -> covers p95 targets with low variance
  * Hosted (pay-as-you-go): slightly higher per-token cost but faster to start and easier for short POCs
(We'll push a precise cost sheet to HubSpot/Deal record tomorrow).

5) Attachments: included a short network-trace sample from our internal perf run to show chunk timings (network-trace-sample.txt).

POC recommendation: 2 weeks, Dedicated trial nodes for performance validation (can fall back to Hosted for dev traffic), sample load test harness and test account, and agreed success criteria on p95/99, error rate, and token cost.

Happy to jump on a technical call with infra next week.

Aditya
